patterns.message: Import the database client only in src/db/repository/ (CLAUDE.md rule 2) — everything else reaches the database through a service, and writes go through withAudit(session, fn). The handful of files that legitimately need a client rather than a writer carry an oxlint-disable-next-line saying why.

Import the repository through its index (`@/db/repository`) — the other files in src/db/repository/ are internal: `selectFrom` is exported only for the finders beside it, and a caller reaching it skips the soft-delete filter (claude-docs/db.md, "Soft-delete filtering"). tests/guards/module-boundaries.test.ts catches the spellings this glob cannot.

Build queries only in src/db/repository/ (CLAUDE.md rule 4) — a Drizzle query cannot be built without importing drizzle-orm at runtime, so this is that rule rather than a style. Reach the database through a service; `import type` is allowed everywhere, which is how the GraphQL layer names Drizzle types (DESIGN.md §7).

This file maps a provider to its env var names — import it only from src/lib/auth.ts or a server component (claude-docs/auth.md, "Social providers"). A client component needs the roster's id/label pairs, which live in social-providers.ts instead; even an env var *name* has no reason to reach the browser bundle. Legitimate imports carry an oxlint-disable-next-line saying why.

Build a DataLoader only through defineLoader (src/graphql/loaders/define-loader.ts) — a loader's cache lives as long as its instance, so one built at module level serves one request's answers to the next (CLAUDE.md rule 9). Register the factory in src/graphql/loaders/index.ts and read the instance off the request context. `import type` is allowed everywhere.

Reach a module through `@/modules/<name>` (its index) or its `schema/` files — its services, GraphQL registrations, loaders and types file are internal, so a deep import is a boundary violation rather than a style (claude-docs/modules.md, "The boundary"). The index re-exports every service the module means to offer; a name missing from it is a decision to make in the module, not to bypass here. tests/guards/module-boundaries.test.ts catches the relative spellings this glob cannot.

paths.name: next/headers
paths.message: A service receives the session as its first argument and never reads the request (claude-docs/auth.md, "Route protection"). The page or GraphQL context calls getSession()/requireSession() and passes the result in.
